sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, 'Autoscale scaling plans and example scenarios in Azure Virtual Desktop'
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'A scaling plan can only operate in its configured time zone'; 'Autoscale only forces users to sign out if you've enabled the force logoff setting during the ramp-down phase'; with force logoff it picks the hosts with the fewest sessions, puts them in drain mode, notifies users, and after a set time 'forcibly signs out any remaining users and turns it off'; 'For pooled host pools, autoscale overwrites drain mode'; a 10% minimum percentage of hosts keeps at least one host available. The ARM reference for Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization/scalingPlans (read 2026-11-18) has timeZone ('Timezone of the scaling plan', required) and, per schedule, rampDownForceLogoffUsers ('Should users be logged off forcefully from hosts').

brief.situation: You are the AVD administrator at Merrow Insurance (Pacific time). Yesterday a colleague assigned a new scaling plan, sp-claims, to the pooled host pool hp-claims: ramp-up 07:00, peak 08:00-17:00, ramp-down 17:00 with force logoff after a 10-minute warning. At 08:30 an agent forwards a pop-up: 'You will be signed out in 30 minutes.' 210 agents are mid-claim.
handover: The colleague created the plan from a template; nobody reviewed it.
A second shift of 90 agents signs in at 10:00 and needs the plan's ramp-up to start more hosts.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the scaling plan's schedule, its time zone and the host pool it controls.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why agents were warned of sign-out at 08:30, what you changed, and what stops a repeat.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: sp-claims was created from a template with time zone UTC; its 17:00 ramp-down with force logoff is 09:00 in Pacific time, so autoscale entered ramp-down and notified users at 08:30.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Fixes the zone, keeps the rest.
parts.modelAnswer: Set the plan's time zone to Pacific Standard Time; it went back to Peak. Deleting the plan would also have stopped the 10:00 ramp-up; drain-mode changes are overwritten by autoscale.

parts.label: Repeat
parts.criteria: Reviews the risky setting and the source.
parts.modelAnswer: Ramp-down now waits for users to sign out until the business agrees otherwise, and the template has no default time zone.

noRampUp.headline: The schedule was right; its clock was wrong
noRampUp.body: A scaling plan works in its configured time zone. Fix the time zone; deleting the plan removes ramp-up as well as ramp-down.

signedOut.headline: 17:00 UTC is 09:00 in Pacific time
signedOut.body: Check a scaling plan's time zone before it runs, and think hard before enabling force logoff.

rescheduled.headline: Good: fixed the clock before it struck
rescheduled.body: You read the plan's time zone and autoscale's phase, fixed the zone without losing ramp-up, checked the next evaluation, and removed both the forced sign-out and the template default.

scoring.modelReasoning: A scaling plan runs in its configured time zone. sp-claims is on UTC, so its 17:00 ramp-down with force logoff starts at 09:00 Pacific, and autoscale has already notified users. Set the time zone to Pacific: peak continues and the 10:00 ramp-up still works. Deleting the plan stops ramp-up too; drain-mode changes are overwritten by autoscale. Then review force logoff with the business and fix the template.
